source.title_on_document: Group-AI collaboration enhances creativity performance: The roles of perspective-taking and AI utilization strategies

supplement.where: Referred to as 'Supplementary Figure 2A' and 'Supplementary Figure 2B' (pp. 12, 15); no URL given
supplement.holds: Full classification schemes for perspective-taking behaviors and AI prompt strategies. Main-text Figure 2 (p. 13) appears to show the same schemes. No creativity statistics are said to sit in the supplement.

paper_design_summary: In a lab experiment in China, 96 university students (analyzed) were randomly paired and each completed a scientific divergent application task (novel uses for a material) under three conditions in counterbalanced order: pair with each member having ChatGPT-4o (group-AI), alone with ChatGPT-4o (individual-AI), and pair without AI (human-only group). Ideas were scored for usefulness and originality by two LLM judges (ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek), and fluency and high-quality idea fluency were counted.

studies.label: Within-subject lab experiment: group-AI vs individual-AI vs human-only group (scientific divergent application task)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Participants were randomly paired into two-person teams; each participant completed all three collaboration modes (group-AI, individual-AI, human-only group), with order of conditions and task items counterbalanced (Figure 1B labels it 'Random Presentation').
assignment.quote: each team was randomly assigned to one of the three collaborative innovation conditions ... The order of conditions and the assignment of tasks were counterbalanced across participants to mitigate potential order and material confounds.

arms.name: Group-AI (G-AI)
arms.description: Two-person team taking turns generating ideas in a shared QQ chat; each member had their own ChatGPT-4o and could ask it one question per own turn.

arms.name: Individual-AI (I-AI)
arms.description: Participant worked one-on-one with ChatGPT-4o; idea panel was private.

arms.name: Human-only group (G)
arms.description: Two-person team taking turns generating ideas in a shared chat; AI interface disabled.

participants.exclusions: 100 recruited via an online questionnaire; 4 excluded for failing to follow task instructions, leaving 96 (64 women). The paper does not say whether the 4 were excluded before or after assignment. Within-subject: each of the 96 contributes to all three arms (96 people = 48 pairs, consistent with F(1, 47) on p. 17).
participants.who: University students; mean age 21.91 (SD 3.51); paid 60 RMB
participants.quote: A total of 100 participants were recruited via an online questionnaire. Four participants were excluded for failing to follow task instructions, resulting in a final sample of 96 (64 women; Mage = 21.91, SD = 3.51).

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4o (OpenAI), accessed via QQ Chat interface
ai_tool.how_used: In group-AI, each member could consult their own ChatGPT-4o once per own turn with a single task-related question; in individual-AI, participant worked one-on-one with ChatGPT-4o (209 group-AI prompts and 313 individual-AI prompts collected). Participants could copy AI ideas verbatim or adapt them.

task.description: Scientific divergent application task (SDAT, adapted from Wan et al. 2025): generate novel applications for a material (transparent ceramics, electronic skin, crystal resin; one item per condition).
task.duration: 15 min per condition (Figure 1B), after a 5-min pre-test questionnaire

outcomes.name: Creative usefulness
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Extent ideas could be realistically applied, 5-point scale, rated by two LLMs (ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek); ICC = 0.74. Analyzed with mixed-effects model, subject ID random effect, condition fixed; control variables (individual creative potential, group preference, algorithm aversion, AI trust) said to be included in analyses. Mediation models (PROCESS Model 4) also report total effects.

contrasts.reported: G-AI M = 4.09, SD = 0.35 vs human-only group M = 3.24, SD = 0.31; fixed effect beta = 0.84, SE = 0.04, p < 0.001; random-effect variance 0.09 (SE = 0.09). Mediation total effect (Fig. 5A) 0.85*** (0.07); direct effect b = 0.77, 95% CI [0.63, 0.91].
contrasts.locator: p. 15, Section 3.1; p. 17, Figure 3A; pp. 19-20, Figure 5A

contrasts.reported: Individual-AI M = 3.34, SD = 0.43 vs human-only group M = 3.24, SD = 0.31; 'No significant difference emerged between the human-only group and individual-AI conditions (p > 0.05).'
G-AI M = 4.09, SD = 0.35 vs individual-AI M = 3.34, SD = 0.43; beta = 0.74, SE = 0.06, p < 0.001. Mediation total effect (Fig. 5D) 0.75*** (0.07).
contrasts.locator: p. 15, Section 3.1; p. 17, Figure 3A; p. 20, Figure 5D

outcomes.name: Creative originality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Rarity of ideas, 5-point scale, rated by ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek; ICC = 0.83. Mixed-effects model with subject random effect.

contrasts.locator: p. 16, Section 3.1; p. 17, Figure 3B; p. 20, Figure 5B

G-AI M = 3.68, SD = 0.50 vs individual-AI M = 2.70, SD = 0.50; beta = 0.98, SE = 0.07, p < 0.001. Mediation total effect (Fig. 5E) 0.97*** (0.09).

outcomes.name: Creative fluency
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of non-redundant ideas. Only a verbal result is reported, with no means or test statistics.

outcomes.name: High-quality idea fluency
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of ideas rated >= 3 on both usefulness and originality by the LLM judges (a count of high-quality ideas, combining fluency and quality). Mixed-effects model with subject random effect.

eligibility.reason: Within-person lab experiment with condition order counterbalanced and described as random (pp. 7-9); 96 people analyzed; usefulness and originality of ideas scored by LLM judges, and counts of ideas. Caveats: 'counterbalanced' order may not be strictly random, and creativity is scored only by LLM judges, not human raters.

one_line_finding: With 96 students in a within-subject lab experiment, pairs whose members each had ChatGPT-4o scored higher than human-only pairs on LLM-rated usefulness (4.09 vs 3.24, beta = 0.84, SE 0.04) and originality (3.68 vs 2.74, beta = 0.94, SE 0.05), while working alone with AI did not differ from human-only pairs (p > 0.05) (pp. 15-16, Figure 3).
open_questions: Independent-samples t-tests comparing group-AI and individual-AI report t(142) (pp. 18-19, 21), which implies about 144 observations, not 96 participants per within-subject condition; the analytic unit for these tests is unclear.

The paper does not say whether the mixed-effects creativity models use one row per idea or one row per participant-condition; unit recorded as participant on the basis of the subject random effect and SD sizes.

Order is called 'counterbalanced' in the text and 'Random Presentation' in Figure 1B; the text also says each team was 'randomly assigned to one of the three conditions' although every participant completed all three.
Whether the four exclusions happened after assignment is not stated.
The journal version (JCAL 2026) may differ; the body text could not be compared.
notes: Process measures (human and AI perspective-taking counts, rate of high-quality adopted ideas, AI usage frequency and prompt strategies, response time) are coded from transcripts and are not creativity outcomes, so they are not listed. Mediation analyses (PROCESS Model 4, pp. 19-21, Figures 5-6) report total, direct, and indirect effects for the three creativity outcomes; total effects from Figure 5 are quoted in the contrasts. Figure 5/6 captions say 'CN' while panels label originality 'CO'. Section 3.3 reports AI usage M = 4.53 (SD 2.40) for group-AI while Section 3.5 reports M = 4.35 (SD 2.40) with the same t(142) = 3.02 but different p and d. No diversity (across-people) outcome is reported. Ethics approval HR2-0252-2024; analyses in SPSS 26.
